concerns_addressed: Media query selectors .nav-hamburger and .nav-links inside @media (max-width: 768px) are now properly scoped to .navbar .nav-hamburger and .navbar .nav-links respectively, preventing unintended style leakage to unrelated elements

strengths: Minimal, surgical fix — only the two media query selectors were changed (2 lines), zero scope creep
The fix directly addresses the scoping concern: responsive hamburger display and nav-links collapse rules now only apply within .navbar context
.navbar.active .nav-links at line 667 was already correctly scoped and required no change
All 37 tests pass after the fix with no regressions
HTML structure is consistent across all 3 pages (login.html, admin.html, display.html) with correct .navbar > .nav-links > .nav-link hierarchy and active class on current page

issues.description: Base selectors .nav-links and .nav-hamburger (outside the media query) remain unscoped. In practice this causes no functional issue because: (1) these class names are only used inside <nav class="navbar"> across all 3 pages, (2) .admin-header .nav-links at line 183 has higher specificity and correctly overrides where needed. However, for full consistency with the media query fix, these could also be scoped to .navbar .nav-links and .navbar .nav-hamburger.

stage_2.assessment: The Cycle 2 fix correctly resolves the primary concern: the responsive media query selectors for .nav-hamburger and .nav-links are now properly scoped to .navbar. The hamburger toggle and mobile collapse behavior will only affect elements within the .navbar component. The two remaining base selectors (.nav-links at line 573, .nav-hamburger at line 599) are unscoped but do not cause any functional or visual issue due to CSS specificity and the fact that these class names are exclusively used in the navbar context. All tests pass. This is a clean, complete fix.
